subject: Cloud Computing
title: Functions as a Service
description: One-minute skill: Functions as a Service.

hook.text: What if you could run one function — not a whole server — and pay only for the milliseconds it runs?

buildup.text: FaaS lets you deploy individual functions. They wake up on an event, execute, then sleep.

discovery.text: AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, and Google Cloud Functions are the major FaaS offerings.

twist.text: Cold starts are the catch. A sleeping function takes extra time to wake up on first request.

climax.text: FaaS is ideal for event-driven tasks: image resizing, webhooks, data processing, scheduled jobs.

punchline.text: One function, one event, one bill. That's FaaS in three words.

quiz.question: What is a 'cold start' in serverless functions?
options: The delay when a sleeping function needs to initialize before handling a request
When a function runs out of memory and crashes
The process of deploying a function for the first time

details.summary: FaaS lets developers deploy individual functions that run in response to events and scale automatically to zero when idle. AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, and Google Cloud Functions charge only for actual execution time, eliminating idle resource costs entirely.
details.whyItMatters: FaaS is the purest form of pay-for-what-you-use computing. It eliminates server management entirely and is ideal for event-driven workloads with variable traffic.
takeaways: Functions execute in response to events like HTTP or queue messages
Billing is per execution with millisecond granularity
Scales to zero when idle, eliminating baseline costs

faq.question: What is cold start latency?
faq.answer: Cold start occurs when a function has not run recently and must be initialized from scratch, adding latency. This can range from 100ms to several seconds depending on runtime and package size. Provisioned concurrency or keeping functions warm mitigates this.

faq.question: What are common FaaS use cases?
faq.answer: API backends, webhook processors, file transformations triggered by uploads, scheduled tasks, IoT data processing, and chat bot handlers are all natural FaaS workloads. Any task that is short-lived and event-triggered is a strong candidate.
